title: Moss and the Hoe
note_for_grown_ups: Non-fiction, Phase 5, 88-sound stage (ew, oe just added).

pages.text: A hoe is a tool to dig with.
pages.illustration: A plain garden hoe leaning against a wooden fence.

pages.text: A hoe has a long stick and a flat end.
pages.illustration: Close view of a hoe's long wooden handle and flat metal end.

pages.text: A hoe can dig up weeds.
pages.illustration: The flat end of a hoe digging up a small weed from the soil.

pages.text: Moss can dig too, but with claws.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog digging in the soil with his own small claws.

pages.text: Moss has sharp claws on his feet.
pages.illustration: Close view of Moss the hedgehog's sharp claws on one foot.

pages.text: Claws are a bit like a hoe.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog's claw next to a hoe's flat end, shown side by side.

pages.text: Moss can dig fast with claws.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog digging quickly, soil flying up behind him.

pages.text: A hoe can dig a long trench.
pages.illustration: A hoe cutting a long straight trench through the soil.

pages.text: Moss can not dig a trench, but he can dig fast.
pages.illustration: Moss the hedgehog digging a smaller, quicker hole beside the long trench.

pages.text: A hoe digs. Sharp claws dig too.
pages.illustration: A hoe and Moss the hedgehog's claws both shown digging in the same patch of soil.
